applied.fix: Explicit class split pinned in four places (Technical Notes bot/carrier bullet, INV-LEARN-4, Infra Prerequisites row, Region ownership note): the weekly job holds a host-held agent-token class scoped exactly {reflect, retain}; the bot-held class keeps M3.1's INV-MEM-1 vocabulary {consolidate, refresh} verbatim; the adds-only scope grant lands on the host-held class only; INV-LEARN-4 adds 'a test asserts the class split'.

applied.finding: Routing-log line shape misattributed to 'R3 facts' — it is not in R3-code-facts.md at all; it lives in J3's own spec (j3-model-router-decision-layer.md:38), and the quoted shape was lossy (score flattened, jev_skipped? dropped). Cross-story drift risk on a consumed read contract.

applied.finding: O_EXCL-create vs replace-per-documentId mechanical conflict: E2E slice required 'O_EXCL + atomic rename' AND 'a re-fire replaces per documentId' — plain O_EXCL fails when the record exists, so the idempotency AC was implementable two contradictory ways (silent stacking or write failure). Also: a shrunken re-fire leaves superseded higher-seq records with no detection path.
applied.fix: Mechanism named: O_EXCL applies to the temp file; a re-fire's replace is a rename-over the existing documentId record, never an in-place rewrite; the fire receipt lists the week's full authoritative documentId set so superseded records stay detectable, never silently authoritative. DOD Contract line aligned.

applied.finding: AC1's policy-ON-while-PROPOSED negative control was structurally unimplementable as written: it required 'a committed policy setting' and a repo-consistency test that 'makes that tree red' — but .factory/ is gitignored (verified .gitignore:97, 'operator-local factory config ... 0600'), so nothing there can be committed and a CI/fresh-checkout consistency test can never observe the ON state. The named HIGH class (ON-while-PROPOSED passing unnoticed) was exactly what the broken mechanism guarded.
applied.fix: Posture corrected in AC1 + AC2 + Technical Notes: the ON setting is operator-local and gitignored by the .factory/ posture (the approvers.json posture), never committed; the consistency test reads the working tree and goes red where the tree lives (operator host, dev lanes); treats a missing or headerless ADR file as PROPOSED; a fresh CI checkout trivially reads OFF because the ON state cannot travel through git — which also means the ON state cannot ride a PR into CI or another lane.

applied.finding: AC4 inertness claim ('with no producer in the tree, no v6a run is auto-merge-eligible — the chain always parks') flatly contradicted the mandatory three-arm demo's 'accepted-eligible labeled proceed' arm: with no producer anywhere, that arm is untestable. Flat reading forces either an untestable AC or a dev silently loosening eligibility.
applied.fix: Production-vs-fixture distinction pinned in AC4 and the DOD inertness line: the inertness test scopes to the production module graph (no real producer); the proceed arm exercises eligibility with a test-fabricated fleet result payload per the A2-owned schema — a fixture, not a producer.

applied.finding: AC4's 'audit-rowed' consumption requirement had no implementation home under the frozen-hop constraint: AUDIT_HOPS (verified, src/audit/link-store.ts:52) contains no QA-verdict hop and no new hop is ever permitted — an unsatisfiable requirement that would surface only at A2 and invite a quiet relaxation.
applied.fix: AC4 pins the meaning: audit-rowed = the verdict is traceable to its producing QA run's audited records (the producing run IS the audit trail; no new hop — AUDIT_HOPS frozen); the exact row mechanism is the A2 producer's to name.

applied.finding: AC1's pre-verdict license ('plus this story's own tests for the fail-closed default') licensed writing loader-arm tests against a policy module that does not exist pre-verdict — red imports in the pre-verdict tree, or an implementer landing the module early to make its tests run (the exact AC1 violation).
applied.fix: AC1 scoped: pre-verdict permitted changes are the verdict block plus repo-state tests only (the consistency and verdict-block tests, which read files and import no policy module); the policy module and its loader-arm tests are implementation and land post-verdict together.

applied.finding: AC3 claimed the classifyDiffScope class vocabulary was 'restated' but never restated it — the AC was not self-contained and pushed the implementer into opening src/fixloop/feedback-run.ts (verified: codes are scope-requires-privilege / out-of-scope-diff), the exact layer-inversion temptation the never-import fence exists to prevent.
applied.fix: AC3 now restates the two codes with their meaning (scope-requires-privilege = deny-glob hit; out-of-scope-diff = no allow match or unpermitted action) and states the boundary: the vocabulary crosses, the fixloop layer does not.
